haiku-low.q1: It gets 401 and never reaches Redis, so no rate-limit counter is read or changed.
haiku-low.q2: The limit belongs to the customer, not the key, so all three keys share one budget: 100 requests per minute for Standard.
haiku-low.q3: A 429 with Retry-After seconds. The request is not forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. Rejected requests increment nothing, so they use no budget.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. An allowed request counts even if the backend then fails, including with a 500.
haiku-low.q6: It fails open: the request is forwarded, ratelimit_store_unavailable is emitted, and X-RateLimit headers are omitted.
haiku-low.q7: Standard is 100 requests per minute. Enterprise is NOT STATED; the limit is undecided, waiting on Product.
haiku-low.q8: Counters live in a shared Redis store under key rl:{customerId}:{minute}. Keys expire after 120 seconds, cleaning up old counts.
haiku-low.q9: At the next fixed clock minute boundary, when the window key changes. The document does not describe other recovery.
haiku-low.q10: check_and_incr is a Lua script Redis runs as one uninterruptible step, checking and incrementing together, so concurrent requests cannot overshoot.
haiku-low.q11: Seconds until the current clock minute ends, at least 1, computed inside the Lua script from Redis server time.
haiku-low.q12: No retry; the request is forwarded and the store is not retried. The client gets no X-RateLimit headers.

sonnet.q1: It gets a 401; Redis is not touched, so no counter is read or changed.
sonnet.q2: Limit belongs to the customer, not the key, so the total across all keys is the customer's single limit (Standard: 100 requests per minute; Enterprise undecided).
sonnet.q3: A 429 with a Retry-After header (seconds until the minute ends). The backend is not called.
sonnet.q4: No. When the count is at the limit nothing is incremented, so 429s use no budget.
sonnet.q5: Yes. An allowed request counts even if the backend fails with 500.
sonnet.q6: Fail open: the Gateway forwards it to the backend anyway, emits ratelimit_store_unavailable, and returns the response without X-RateLimit headers.
sonnet.q7: Standard is 100 requests per minute. Enterprise is NOT STATED (not decided yet, Product owns it).
sonnet.q8: In shared Redis, in a counter key rl:{customerId}:{minute}. Keys expire after 120 seconds, so old counters clean themselves up.
sonnet.q9: It resets when the fixed clock minute ends; a new minute uses a new counter key (the old one expires after 120 s).
sonnet.q10: The check_and_incr Lua script checks the count and increments in one uninterruptible step in Redis, so concurrent requests on different instances cannot overshoot the limit.
sonnet.q11: It is the number of seconds until the current minute ends (at least 1), computed in the Lua script from Redis time.
sonnet.q12: No retry (a retry or queue was deliberately not added). The client gets the backend response with no X-RateLimit-* headers.
